item.title: Multiple education scholarships available
item.description: LIHUE — Applications for the Delta Kappa Gamma Kauai ETA Chapter Education Scholarships are currently being accepted, the Delta Kappa Gamma Kauai ETA Chapter announced Tuesday.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Gov eyes housing, health, fiscal cuts
item.description: Managing the economy during turbulent times is like that metaphor about building an airplane while it’s in flight. Conditions are changing in unpredictable ways, and plans made even a short time ago start to show gaps.

item.title: Hawaii coalition calls for tax fairness for local needs
item.description: As Hawaii struggles to meet growing needs in housing, education, health care and climate resilience, a broad coalition of community groups, labor unions and nonprofit advocates is pushing lawmakers to confront a long-standing question: how to pay for it.

item.title: Homeless count illustrates gaps in the system
item.description: For the first time since 2024, Oahu on Monday resumed its unsheltered Point in Time count of people living on the streets. Outreach teams, service providers and city officials fanned out across Honolulu — including Chinatown, one of the island’s most visible areas of homelessness.

item.title: 40 years after Challenger disaster, Hawaii’s Ellison Onizuka remembered as a trailblazer
item.description: As the nation commemorates the anniversary of the Challenger space shuttle disaster, here in the islands some members of the community have been paying tribute to crew member Ellison Onizuka — who is both the first Asian American and the first person from Hawaii to go to space.
